card.occupation: Retired. Worked 27 years as a medical secretary at a GP practice in Norton, and took early retirement at 63 on her NHS pension.
card.education_detail: Left a comprehensive school in Stockton at 16 with O levels in English, Maths, Typing and Biology. Did a one-year secretarial course at the local technical college and later an AMSPAR medical terminology certificate through evening classes in her thirties.
card.household: Lives in a two-bedroom ex-council semi she bought under Right to Buy with her ex-husband, and kept after their divorce in 2004. Her son Daniel, 31, moved back in two years ago after his relationship ended. He works shifts at a distribution warehouse near Teesport. Her daughter Rebecca lives in Leeds with her partner and toddler.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Stockton. Her dad was a fitter at the ICI works at Billingham and her mam was a dinner lady. She was christened Church of England and goes to her parish church most Sundays, more for the quiet and the familiar faces than for any strong views. She helps with the church coffee morning once a month.
card.professional_persona: She was the person at the surgery who knew where everything was filed and which patients needed a gentler phone call. She was precise, discreet and reliable, and was never interested in becoming practice manager when the job came up. She still keeps her own household paperwork in labelled box files.
card.sports_persona: She isn't sporty, but she walks most mornings along the riverside by the Tees Barrage, about forty minutes and usually alone. She half-follows Middlesbrough's results because Daniel has the match on, and doesn't pretend otherwise.
card.arts_persona: She reads a lot, mostly crime series and family sagas, borrowed from the library or picked up from charity shops. She likes period dramas on the telly and once went to see a play at the ARC in Stockton with a friend from church. Music is mostly Radio 2 in the kitchen.
card.travel_persona: She has no great urge to go far. She takes a caravan week in Filey or Northumberland most years, and has been on a couple of coach holidays to the Lake District and once to the Scottish Highlands. She has been abroad only a handful of times, to Spain with the kids when they were small and once to Majorca with her sister in 2018. She drives to Leeds every few weeks to see her grandson.
card.culinary_persona: She is a plain, steady cook: mince and dumplings, a Sunday dinner, corned beef pie, a stew in the slow cooker on Daniel's late shifts. Tea is at half five unless he's working. She bakes a tray bake for the church coffee morning and is quietly proud of her lemon drizzle. She has a parmo from the takeaway maybe twice a year and feels guilty about it.
hobbies_and_interests: Reading crime novels and family sagas
Looking after her small back garden, mainly pots and hanging baskets
Puzzle magazines and the crossword in the paper
Looking after her grandson in Leeds when she visits
skills: Medical terminology from her old job
Keeping calm on the phone with upset or difficult people
Basic computer use, including email, online banking and the NHS app
card.career_goals: None in terms of paid work. She is content being retired. She has thought about volunteering a morning a week at the hospice charity shop, and probably will once she gets round to ringing them. Mostly she wants to keep her health, help Daniel get back on his feet and see more of her grandson.
card.voice: Quiet, measured and fairly soft-spoken, with a Teesside accent that is clear but not broad. She speaks in complete, careful sentences and pauses to think before answering rather than filling the gap. She uses 'erm' when she's choosing her words and 'sort of' as a softener. She says 'mam', 'tea' for the evening meal, and occasionally 'yous' when talking about her kids. She is polite and says 'sorry, could you say that again?' if she mishears. She's comfortable with a short silence and won't rush to fill it, and she sometimes finishes an answer with 'if that makes sense'. She gives short answers at first and opens up a bit if the conversation is warm.
card.typing: Proper sentences with capital letters and full stops, apostrophes used correctly, and no text-speak or emojis. She occasionally uses a double space after a full stop out of old typing habit. Answers are brief but complete, for example: 'I walk most mornings, usually about 40 minutes.' She will go back and correct a typo.
card.with_strangers: Reserved but courteous. She can seem a little guarded or shy at first and answers what's asked without offering much extra. She is honest to the point of saying 'I don't really know' rather than guessing. She warms up slowly and comes across as sensible, kind and slightly self-effacing. She doesn't like to make a fuss or talk herself up.
small_things: The weather on her morning walk and the herons by the Barrage
Whatever crime book she's halfway through
Daniel's shift pattern and whether she's doing tea early or late
Her hanging baskets and the slugs
The church coffee morning and who made what
The price of things at Asda compared to last year
deeper_things: The divorce came after years of her ex-husband's drinking. She stayed longer than she should have for the kids' sake.
She worries about Daniel. He has been low since his break-up, and she is careful not to nag him.
She sometimes feels lonely in the evenings, even with Daniel in the house, and misses her mam, who died in 2016.
She doesn't see Rebecca and the baby as often as she'd like, and doesn't want to be a burden by asking.
Her faith is more of a comfort than a certainty, and she has had doubts, especially after her mam's long illness.
She is quietly proud that she kept the house and raised two kids on a secretary's wage.
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a dining table, angled slightly upward so the ceiling edge is just visible. Daylight comes from a window to her left, lighting that side of her face more evenly than the other. She is a white woman in her mid-sixties with a pale complexion, light freckling and fine lines around her eyes. Her expression is a small polite closed-mouth smile and she looks slightly past the camera at the screen. Her hair is short, ash-blonde with grey coming through, neatly cut and brushed back from her face. She wears thin gold-rimmed reading glasses and a lilac crew-neck jumper over a white collared blouse, with a small gold cross on a fine chain. Behind her is a magnolia wall with a framed photo of a toddler in a blue coat, a wall calendar from a local charity with handwritten entries, and the corner of a glass-fronted cabinet holding china plates and a couple of trophies. A spider plant sits on top of the cabinet.
